extracted.intended_audience: Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) licensees, their officers/managers, counsel and auditors
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements governing SBIC licensees' transactions, recordkeeping, reporting, internal controls, insurance, exemptions, and interpretations of eligible financing. Focused on post-licensing compliance, financial reporting and safeguarding of assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and copy to SBA for affected locality
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee shall publish notice to the locality most directly affected by the transaction, in form specified by SBA, and shall furnish a copy to SBA within 10 days after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where SBA requires public notice; copy must be provided to SBA within ten days of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1940 Act companies — exemption notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1940 Act company granted an exemption by the SEC for a transaction subject to paragraph (b) shall be exempt from the provisions thereof: Provided, however, That such Licensee shall inform SBA of the exemption and shall cause prompt public notice thereof, in form specified by SBA, to be published in a newspaper of general circulation and shall furnish SBA a copy of such notice within 10 days after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if exempt from certain SBA provisions due to SEC exemption, the Licensee must notify SBA and publish/present proof of public notice within 10 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of investment — serving as officer/director
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee may permit any of its Associates, an employee, or representative from serving as an officer, director, or in any other capacity in management of a small business concern for purpose of protecting its investment: Provided, however, That the person so designated has no other direct or indirect financial interest in the portfolio concern and has not served as an officer or director or in any other capacity in the management of such concern for more than 30 days prior to such financing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted only to protect investment; prerequisite: no other financial interest and limited prior management service (<=30 days prior to financing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sale of portfolio securities to Associates
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where a written exemption may be granted by SBA in special instances, a Licensee shall not dispose of its portfolio securities to any of its Associates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As prerequisite to an exemption, Licensee must demonstrate that the proposed sale's terms are no less favorable than those obtainable elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sale of portfolio securities to competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where specifically approved in writing by the portfolio small concern not controlled by the Licensee or where granted a prior written exemption by SBA, a Licensee shall not dispose of the portfolio securities of a concern to a competitor of such small concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All sales by Licensees of portfolio securities to competitors must have relevant particulars promptly reported to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess real estate investments for SBICs licensed prior to March 19, 1965
rubrics_metrics.description: SBICs licensed prior to March 19, 1965 whose real estate investments as of March 31, 1965, exceeded one-third of their portfolio may retain such investments (if not consummated in violation when made) but shall not undertake further real estate investments until portfolio diversified so real estate portion constitutes less than one-third in dollar amount of total portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After diversification below one-third, new real estate investments may be made subject to §107.1001(c) and the one-third limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Government sponsorship representation
rubrics_metrics.description: No Licensee in issuing any security shall represent or imply in any manner that such security has been approved by the United States, or any agency or officer thereof, and a statement to such effect shall be included in any solicitations to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All solicitations must include a disclaimer that the security is not Government-approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations — nonperformance of agreements with SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonperformance by a Licensee of any of the terms, conditions, or requirements of any debenture, loan agreement, note, or other written agreement with SBA constitutes a violation of the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to perform contractual obligations to SBA is a regulatory violation and actionable under enforcement provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations — false statements or omissions to SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any false statement knowingly made, or misrepresentation or failure to state a material fact necessary to make the statement not misleading, in any document submitted by a Licensee to SBA pursuant to applicable provisions of the Act or regulations constitutes a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers knowingly false statements and material omissions in submissions to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — current financial records and GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall keep current financial records in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, including the maintenance of books of account in accordance with the System of Account Classifications prescribed by SBA as set forth in Part 111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain financial records and minutes of meetings, and files containing pertinent transaction documents at principal place of business, except portfolio items held by custodian under written agreement. Financial reports to SBA must make full and complete disclosure of matters relevant to the Act and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of records — permanently accessible first two years
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve permanently, the first 2 years in an easily accessible place, (i) all general and subsidiary ledgers (or other records) reflecting all asset and valuation, liability, capital stock and surplus, income, and expense accounts; (ii) all general and special journals (or other records forming the basis for entries) and corporate charter, bylaws, Proposal to Operate, minute books, capital stock certificates or stubs, stock ledgers, and stock transfer registers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These core records must be permanently preserved with the first two years immediately accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of records — six-year retention for loan/investment documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve for a period of not less than 6 years following repayment, sale, or other final disposition of the related loan or investment (the first 2 years in an easily accessible place) all applications for financing, size status declarations, lending agreements, participation agreements, escrow agreements, financing instruments, capital stock certificates and warrants of small business concerns not surrendered or exercised, and all other documents and supporting material relating to such loan or investment, including correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record retention timeline ties to disposition of each loan/investment; first two years must be easily accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of accounting source documents — six years
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve for a period of not less than six (6) years all vouchers, checkbooks, bank statements, cancelled checks, cash reconciliations, ledger trial balances, memoranda, correspondence, and other documents forming the initial accounting data for entry in, or underlying records in support of, the records enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers source documents supporting accounting records; six-year minimum retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic substitution for originals after three years
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the foregoing, after any book, document, or other record has been preserved for three (3) years (or 3 years following final disposition of the related loan or investment, when applicable), a photograph or film thereof may be substituted therefor for the balance of the required time and the original destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits microfilm/photographic copies after three years subject to retention period requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports to stockholders — filing with SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time any financial report (including any prospectus, letter, or other publication with respect to the financial affairs or operations of the Licensee or any of its portfolio small business concerns) is furnished to investors and shareholders of a Licensee, such Licensee shall file with the Office of Investment, SBA, three (3) copies of such report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triplicate filing required concurrently with distribution to investors/shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reports to SBA — periodic filing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall submit to SBA, at the end of the first 6-month period of each fiscal year, a report containing financial statements covering such 6-month period; at the end of each fiscal year a report containing financial statements for the fiscal year; and, when requested by SBA, interim financial reports. The fiscal year for SBA purposes is April 1 through March 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic filing schedule: semiannual and annual reports, plus interim reports upon request; SBA fiscal year fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual audit and accountant's opinion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The report as of the end of each fiscal year shall contain, or be accompanied by, an independent public accountant’s opinion on the financial statements for the fiscal year included therein, unless a different 12-month period to be covered by the annual audit is expressly given prior approval in writing by SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion must be based on an audit conducted in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards and SBA's Audit and Examination Guide, by an independent CPA or licensed public accountant selected/approved by SBA; alternative for jurisdictions without licensing requires an independent public accountant of recognized standing with 10+ years public accounting experience and SBA approval (with pre- Sept 8, 1967 grandfathering noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and filing deadlines for financial reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial reports required to be filed with SBA shall be on SBA Form 468 (9-67), filed in triplicate with the Office of Investment, SBA, on or before the last day of the month immediately following the close of the period covered by the report (unaudited), and on or before the last day of the third month following the close of the period covered by the report (audited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed form SBA Form 468 (9-67) and comply with triplicate filing and the separate deadlines for unaudited vs audited reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1940 Act company financial reporting cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees which are 1940 Act companies should refer to rules promulgated by the SEC for requirements as to financial reports to be filed with SEC and the time allowed for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1940 Act companies follow SEC rules for SEC filings; still must provide required info to SBA as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reports must present fairly and follow SBA instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Financial Report filed by each Licensee shall present fairly the financial position of the Licensee as of the close of the period covered and the results of operations, and shall be prepared in accordance with the Instructions for Preparation of the Financial Report, SBA Form 468 (9-67) (Instructions identified as SBA Form 468A (1-68)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions printed in Appendix 2 and obtain forms from SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Evaluation Report (SBA Form 684) annual filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Evaluation Report, SBA Form 684 (1-68), shall be prepared by each Licensee as of March 31 of every calendar year and filed in triplicate with SBA not later than June 30, to reflect all transactions involving Licensee’s debt or equity financing of small business concerns outstanding at any time during the preceding 12-month period ending March 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare per Instructions (SBA Form 684A); copies available from SBA. Information is for SBA official use and not for public disclosure except statistical totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee’s condition to require portfolio information for Form 684
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall, as a condition of all financing agreements consummated or renegotiated with small business concerns after March 25, 1966, require such concerns to furnish to the Licensee all information needed for preparation and filing of SBA Form 684.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee must contractually obtain necessary portfolio information from investees for program evaluation reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of Program Evaluation Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of Part 102 prohibiting disclosure of information in SBA files apply to Program Evaluation Reports; information submitted on SBA Form 684 is for SBA official use and not for public disclosure except in statistical totals or summaries not divulging identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data is protected from public release; only aggregated statistics may be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Licensee which is a party in any capacity to litigation or other proceedings shall within 10 days of becoming a party file a report with SBA describing the nature and status of the proceedings, the identity of and Licensee’s relationship to other parties, and, upon SBA’s request, submit copies of pleadings and other specified documents. If proceedings are compromised/settled or final judgment entered, Licensee shall furnish SBA a statement of terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely (10-day) reporting of litigation or proceedings is required; include identity/relationship and provide documents on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent filing with SBA of SEC filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a Licensee files any report, application or document with the SEC, it shall concurrently provide SBA with a copy thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA must receive contemporaneous copies of SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to file other reports upon SBA request
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to other required reports, each Licensee shall, upon request by SBA, file with the Office of Investment such other reports at such times and in such forms as SBA shall require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA has authority to require additional reporting as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control — adoption of organization plan and control measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall adopt a plan of organization and coordinate methods and measures designed to safeguard its assets and check the accuracy and reliability of its financial data. Effective control arrangements shall be established and maintained covering the Licensee’s personnel, portfolio of investment securities, funds, and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires formal internal control system tailored to safeguard assets and ensure financial data integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual control over disbursements and safekeeping withdrawals
rubrics_metrics.description: With specified exceptions, each Licensee shall maintain dual control over disbursement of funds and withdrawal of securities from safekeeping. Disbursements shall be made only by means of checks requiring signatures of two or more officers of the Licensee, covered by the Licensee’s fidelity bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: separate imprest bank account rules (aggregate balance limit, reimbursement via dual-signature check); checks ≤ $1,000 drawn on imprest may be signed by any authorized bonded officer. Opening safe deposit boxes or withdrawing securities requires two or more bonded officers or one bonded officer and one bonded employee. Furnish certified copy of board resolution establishing these procedures to depository banks/custodians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity insurance — mandatory bond coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall maintain a fidelity bond in the form and amount set forth by SBA in its Audit and Examination Guide, executed by an acceptable surety; each officer and employee who has control over or access to cash, securities or other property shall be covered by such fidelity bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond must be from a surety holding a certificate of authority acceptable for Federal bonds per Title 6; covers officers/employees with asset access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity bond cancellation notification and claims reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee, at least 30 days prior to making any request to the surety to terminate or cancel the bond, shall notify SBA in writing of its intent; the bond must contain a rider requiring the surety to notify SBA of intent to cancel or expiration at least 30 days in advance. Each Licensee shall notify SBA immediately in writing of any claim for loss filed under the bond with the surety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects SBA's interest by ensuring advance notice of bond termination and immediate reporting of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting postlicensing changes (non-change-of-control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change of Licensee’s name, address, operating area, charter, bylaws, increase in capitalization, financing plans, investment policy, officers, directors, or other changes not covered by §107.701 or for which prior approval is not specifically required shall be reported to SBA not later than thirty (30) days after the events described. All changes shall be subject to SBA postapproval as a condition for continuance of the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-day notice requirement; reported changes are subject to SBA review and possible conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA approval presumed unless notified within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and requests filed pursuant to postlicensing change provisions shall be deemed approved unless Licensee is notified to the contrary by SBA within ninety (90) days after receipt. SBA approval is contingent upon full disclosure of all relevant facts and may be subject to conditions SBA determines reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silence for 90 days is deemed approval but approval may be conditioned and requires full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from civil penalties — impracticability application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is impracticable for a Licensee to submit any required report within the time limit, the president or CEO may prior to the filing date present a written application identifying the report, certifying extraordinary events making submission impracticable due to no fault of the Licensee, and accompanied by written evidence. SBA may exempt the Licensee in whole or in part from civil penalties section 315(a) for such length and upon such conditions as SBA determines reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application should be submitted promptly after occurrence; SBA has discretion to grant exemptions and impose conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'impracticable' for penalty exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: For this section, 'impracticable' refers to conditions making it physically impossible or otherwise unreasonable for a prudent businessman to prepare and file the required report on time. Such conditions include death or serious illness of Licensee’s key personnel, or unavoidable loss or destruction of books, records or other data by fire, theft, or similar hazards beyond Licensee’s control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets narrow, practical meaning tied to extraordinary, uncontrollable events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from regulatory provisions — application and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee may file an application in writing with SBA to have a proposed action, subject to any procedural or substantive requirement, restriction, or prohibition under this part, exempted from applicable provisions. SBA may approve such application conditionally or unconditionally to the extent that such requirement is not prescribed by statute and exemption would not be contrary to the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include supporting evidence demonstrating (a) terms of proposed action are fair and equitable; and (b) exemption requested is reasonably calculated to advance best interests of the SBIC program consistent with policy objectives of the Act and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savings clause for prior transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions of a continuing nature consummated with third parties prior to January 9, 1968 pursuant to former provisions shall be governed by such former provisions; SBA may take or continue enforcement action with respect to any transaction consummated prior to January 9, 1968 in violation of former provisions applicable at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves legal effect of transactions under prior rules but does not bar enforcement of past violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital structure — fairness and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever capitalization consists of more than one class of stock, the voting rights and other rights and remedies may not be inequitable or discriminatory, and may not unduly concentrate control or management through pyramiding, inequitable methods, or inequitable distribution. Full disclosure of all voting rights and other rights and remedies of all classes of stock must be made to all shareholders prior to their purchase of stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires equitable capital structures and pre-purchase disclosure to shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural enterprise financing prohibition and classification rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 107.1001(i) prohibits a Licensee from financing concerns engaged solely or primarily in production of agricultural commodities (field crops, livestock, nursery crops). A concern engaged in both agricultural and business enterprise is classified according to the predominant part of its operations considering time devoted and income derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of eligibility for mixed-activity concerns is based on predominance (time and income).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification of retained earnings as capital via stock dividend
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may increase paid-in capital and paid-in surplus by capitalizing accumulated unappropriated retained earnings through issuance of a stock dividend: Provided, however, That the per share value of the stock dividend issued shall be the higher of fair value or the average paid-in capital per share existing at the time the dividend is declared (par or stated value plus paid-in surplus divided by number of shares issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The increased paid-in capital and surplus may be included in total paid-in capital and used to determine the amount of debentures SBA may purchase per §§107.201 and 107.202.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess section 303(b) funds from mergers — repayment obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate amount of debentures SBA may purchase may not exceed statutory limits. If a merger consummated without revision of constituent capital accounts results in excess SBA funds, the excessive debenture amount must be repaid to SBA within a reasonable period of time; Licensee may demonstrate what constitutes a reasonable period by appropriate evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee afforded opportunity to justify proposed repayment schedule based on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated concerns treated as single entity for financing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: By reason of common ownership and control, affiliated corporations constitute a single small business concern for purposes of financing limits; the total amount of Licensee’s financing may not exceed its statutory loan and investment limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliation rules aggregate related entities for size and financing limit determinations (example provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum amortization limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 107.301(a) does not require equal annual amortization but prohibits amortization to accumulate at a rate in excess of 20 percent per annum. Total amortization divided by the number of years elapsed may not, at any point, exceed 20 percent of principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate permissible scheduling (e.g., 10% first year, 30% second year permitted if cumulative average ≤20%) and impermissible schedules (30% first year, 10% second year not permitted unless within Special Discretionary Portfolio limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term loans to protect Licensee's investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term advances made to a portfolio concern when reasonably necessary to protect Licensee’s existing long-term investment are authorized under §107.301(d); e.g., a short-term loan to a surviving concern of a merger to reorganize debt may be regarded as reasonably necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to avoid formal reorganization or bankruptcy where the survivor meets size eligibility standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC financing for radio and television stations
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIC financing for radio and television stations is permissible; SBIC loans/investments are privately owned and not Government loans, and therefore such financing would not be considered 'contrary to the public interest' under §107.1061(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes SBIC program from SBA 7(a) policy prohibitions on loans to broadcasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase of existing notes to protect investment — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may acquire an outstanding promissory note, debenture, or other indebtedness of its portfolio concern when necessary to protect existing long-term investment. Licensee may disburse funds directly to a creditor in exchange for assignment where funds represent an eligible loan for bona fide small business purposes for minimum term of 5 years. If unexpired term of outstanding debt is less than 5 years, purchase unauthorized unless within Special Discretionary Portfolio limits. Licensee shall keep on file loan application or document evidencing portfolio concern's request and a completed SBA Form 480, Size Status Declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum of amounts paid for acquisition plus existing long-term investment may not exceed 20 percent limit in §107.301(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans secured by real estate — functional test
rubrics_metrics.description: A loan or investment secured by liens against real estate is not necessarily a 'real estate investment' within §107.3; determination depends on nature of business activities and end-use of proceeds. Example: a manufacturing concern's loan secured by real estate mortgage would not be classified as real estate investment unless changed circumstances cause gross receipts from real estate to exceed manufacturing receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify based on recipient's business activity and end-use, not solely on collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment leasing vs rental service concerns — classification and financing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment leasing concerns (special equipment acquired for particular lessee, long-term lease, lessee furnishes maintenance, provision to obtain title at end) typically cannot meet §107.1001(a) and (f) requirements and thus may not be financed. Rental service concerns (inventory of equipment rented/re-rented to different parties, short-term rental, maintenance facilities, repossession at term end, no nominal-title acquisition) may meet requirements and may be financed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees may not finance 'equipment leasing concerns' as defined, but may invest in 'rental service concerns' that meet §107.1001 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and Examination Guide as regulatory standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Audit and Examination Guide for Small Business Investment Companies (Revised Jan. 9, 1968) is printed in Appendix 1 as part of the regulations of this part and sets forth required forms, fidelity bond amounts, and audit procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent audits and fidelity bond amounts and forms must conform to the Guide; auditors should perform audits with uniformly high competency per Foreword.
